supplementaryReferences.title: Edible-part and safety review
supplementaryReferences.quote: There are conflicting reports on the toxicity of the fruit, both green and ripe.
supplementaryReferences.note: SANBI reports culinary uses but also toxic constituents and poisoning concerns. A preparation report is not a complete safe household recipe.

productionGuidance.products: traditionally prepared leaves/fruit — specialist review needed
care: Retain this climber in mapped inventory, but do not count it as normal household food until a qualified local specialist confirms identity, edible part and safe preparation.
SANBI records it across South Africa except Western Cape, in varied habitats.
purchase: Resolve food-use and preparation with an experienced local food-plant specialist before buying it as a household crop.

sourceChecks.observations: Read indexed primary SANBI page content. Direct PlantZAfrica requests in this audit returned HTTP 403; this is not a claim that every individual endpoint was live-tested.

gaps: October–May mainly flowering/fruiting is not a confirmed safe ripe-food window. No safe recipe, measured food yield or planting-to-food interval.
